title: Which Azure ETL tool fits you?

questions.hint: This one answer removes about half the list.

options.label: Microsoft Fabric (OneLake)
options.why: you land in Fabric, and Lakeflow Connect writes into Databricks instead

options.label: Azure Databricks
options.why: Databricks is where your analysts work

options.label: Azure Synapse or Azure SQL
options.why: your target is not Databricks, and Lakeflow Connect writes Delta streaming tables into Databricks

options.label: Files in my own Azure Data Lake Storage
options.why: ADF can write Iceberg to ADLS Gen2, Fivetran's docs say its lake service writes Parquet there, OLake Go's Azure guide writes Iceberg to ADLS Gen2, and Hevo lists no ADLS destination in the docs we read

questions.q: How do you want to pay and run it?

options.label: Free software that I host myself
options.why: Airbyte Core is free to self-host and you pay for servers and staff, and OLake Go is open source under Apache 2.0 and runs on your own infrastructure

options.label: Pay per use, with no capacity kept running
options.why: ADF bills per run and per compute hour

options.label: A Fabric capacity is fine
options.why: both Fabric options bill through a running Fabric capacity

options.label: A vendor runs it all, no servers
Many SaaS apps
options.why: you need a long connector list

options.label: Databases that I want kept in sync
options.why: you want database changes copied over, and OLake Go's docs cover Azure Database for PostgreSQL and MySQL Flexible Server

options.label: SSIS packages or a private network
options.why: Microsoft lists SSIS and managed virtual networks as To be determined in Fabric, and ADF supports them

questions.q: What should happen to the data on the way?

options.label: A live, read-only copy for reports
options.why: mirroring gives a read-only copy with no pipelines

options.label: Load it raw on a schedule, reshape later
options.why: you want ELT with incremental loads

options.label: Clean or audit it before it lands
options.why: mirroring has a single read-only destination and no transforms

questions.q: How big is your team and estate?

options.label: Small team, I want posted prices
options.why: Hevo and ADF publish their rates

options.label: Somewhere in the middle
options.why: you have no strong need either way

options.label: Large and regulated, a sales quote is fine
options.why: Informatica publishes no dollar price per unit, so expect a quote, and its docs list several Azure replication targets

fabric.name: Fabric Copy job
fabric.summary: Scheduled full, incremental or CDC copies into OneLake without building pipelines.
fabric.bestWhen: Fabric is your analytics home and you want scheduled, incremental loads.
fabric.watchOut: CDC is in preview and leaves out PostgreSQL, MySQL and MongoDB, and SSIS and managed private networks are not there yet.

mirroring.name: Fabric mirroring
mirroring.summary: A continuously updated, read-only copy of a database in OneLake, with free replication compute.
mirroring.bestWhen: you want a live copy of a supported database for Fabric reports.
mirroring.watchOut: a Fabric capacity must keep running, and it writes to one read-only destination with no custom scheduling or transforms.

adf.name: Azure Data Factory
adf.summary: Microsoft's pay-per-use pipeline service for hybrid ETL, with SSIS support and a self-hosted runtime.
adf.bestWhen: you run SSIS, need a private network or already have ADF pipelines.
adf.watchOut: Microsoft says to start with Fabric Data Factory if you are new, and new Fabric features are not backported.

lakeflow.name: Databricks Lakeflow Connect
lakeflow.summary: Managed connectors that copy database changes into Databricks Delta tables.
lakeflow.bestWhen: Databricks is where your analysts work.
lakeflow.watchOut: the gateway is paid even when idle, the MySQL connector is Public Preview, and MongoDB is not listed.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: Open-source replication of Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB and SQL Server (plus Oracle, Db2, S3 and Kafka sources) into Iceberg or Parquet, with an Azure guide for ADLS Gen2.
olake.bestWhen: your sources are databases and you want Iceberg or Parquet on Azure storage you run.
olake.watchOut: its output is Iceberg and Parquet, so it suits teams that want one of those on storage they run.

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A fully managed ELT service with many connectors and a free plan up to a row limit.
fivetran.bestWhen: you want a vendor to run everything and your row counts are predictable.
fivetran.watchOut: billing is by monthly active rows, deletes count as paid rows, and its lake service has no Iceberg position deletes.

hevo.name: Hevo
hevo.summary: A managed ELT service with posted tiers and a free plan.
hevo.bestWhen: a small team loads a Synapse dedicated pool and wants posted prices.
hevo.watchOut: its docs name dedicated SQL pools as the Synapse destination, and we found no Fabric or ADLS destination.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: A free self-hosted Core edition plus a paid cloud, with a long connector list.
airbyte.bestWhen: you want to self-host, or land data in Databricks or SQL Server.
airbyte.watchOut: its Azure Blob destination lists CSV and JSON Lines only, with no Synapse page, and database capture runs as scheduled syncs.

informatica.name: Informatica
informatica.summary: An enterprise data management suite whose replication docs list ADLS Gen2, Synapse, Fabric and OneLake targets.
informatica.bestWhen: you run a large, regulated estate with a dedicated team.
informatica.watchOut: no dollar price per unit is published, so you need a quote from Informatica.
